claude.sample_unit: prescriptions of older patients with diabetes (60 medication plans rated by 12 specialists)

links.outcome: Expert-rated medication schedule accuracy and safety: evidence-database-constrained system vs ungrounded GPT-4
links.effect: DUMS vs GPT-4 accuracy 4.43 vs 3.84 and safety 4.44 vs 3.91 (both P<.001); total score 37.96 vs 36.35 (P<.001).
links.quote: The evaluation results revealed that the DUMS group achieved significantly higher accuracy and safety scores than the GPT-4 group ( P <.001), with full consideration of multiple aspects of DDI, pharmacokinetics, and dietary restrictions.

links.outcome: Head-to-head expert ratings of DUMS, pharmacist-refined output, and GPT-4 on same prescriptions
links.effect: Total scores: DUMS 37.96, intervention 39.52, GPT-4 36.35 (all pairwise P<.001); DUMS outperformed GPT-4 on accuracy, safety, comprehensiveness, richness.
links.quote: The total evaluation scores showed that the mean values of the DUMS group, intervention group, and GPT-4 group were 37.96 (SD 0.56), 39.52 (SD 0.80), and 36.35 (SD 0.89), respectively.

unlisted_practices: Pharmacist refinement of system-generated medication schedules improved adherence, usefulness, comprehensiveness and richness scores

links.effect: Total scores: DUMS 37.96 (SD 0.56), intervention 39.52 (SD 0.80), GPT-4 36.35 (SD 0.89); P<.001.
links.quote: The total evaluation scores showed that the mean values of the DUMS group, intervention group, and GPT-4 group were 37.96 (SD 0.56), 39.52 (SD 0.80), and 36.35 (SD 0.89), respectively.

links.effect: Intervention total score 39.52 (SD 0.80) versus DUMS 37.96 (SD 0.56) and GPT-4 36.35 (SD 0.89); P<.001.
links.quote: The “adjusted” DUMS results (ie, the intervention group) were better than those of the other groups, with statistically significant differences ( P <.001), as shown in Table 3 .

links.effect: Grounded DUMS accuracy 4.43 vs GPT-4 3.84; safety 4.44 vs 3.91; both P<.001.
links.quote: The evaluation results revealed that the DUMS group achieved significantly higher accuracy and safety scores than the GPT-4 group ( P <.001), with full consideration of multiple aspects of DDI, pharmacokinetics, and dietary restrictions.

Reliability analysis demonstrated that the DUMS group outperformed the GPT-4 group in medication schedule accuracy and safety, as well as comprehensiveness and richness of the self-management program (P<.001).

links.outcome: medication schedule and self-management program performance compared to software and clinicians
links.effect: DUMS and pharmacist refinement scored significantly higher than GPT-4 in schedule accuracy (4.43 and 4.49 vs 3.84), safety (4.44 vs 3.91), and total scores (37.96 and 39.52 vs 36.35; all P<.001).
links.quote: Reliability analysis demonstrated that the DUMS group outperformed the GPT-4 group in medication schedule accuracy and safety, as well as comprehensiveness and richness of the self-management program (P<.001).

unlisted_practices: pharmacist refinement of automated medication schedule outputs
